score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 7 major vendors (BizProspex, Thomson Data, ContactOut, BookYourData, LakeB2B, AverickMedia, Blue Mail Media) currently selling attorney/lawyer databases ranging from 53K to 1.5M+ records with pricing from $200-$295 baseline for mid-volume lists. Five high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) legal technology vendors (Clio, MyCase, PracticePanther, CosmoLex, Smokeball) selling practice management software, case management, time tracking, and billing platforms at $39-$129/month per attorney — LegalTech vendors pay $5,000-$15,000/year for targeted attorney marketing lists to acquire customers with $500-$1,500/year LTV; (2) continuing legal education (CLE) providers selling mandatory state-required courses — all attorneys must complete 10-15 hours of CLE annually (state-dependent) to maintain bar membership, creating recurring $300-$800/year spend per attorney; (3) legal research platforms (Fastcase, Casetext, vLex) competing with Westlaw/LexisNexis by offering lower-cost research tools at $65-$150/month to solo/small firm practitioners; (4) legal insurance and malpractice carriers (The Bar Plan, ALPS, CNA) selling professional liability coverage required by many states for practice — premiums range $1,500-$8,000/year per attorney depending on practice area and coverage limits; and (5) legal marketing agencies, SEO firms, and lead generation platforms targeting personal injury, family law, criminal defense, and estate planning attorneys who spend $2,000-$20,000/month on client acquisition. All 50 states plus DC maintain public attorney license registries via their State Bar Associations or Supreme Court licensing divisions, accessible through state-specific websites with no authentication required for lookup. Data includes attorney full name, bar number, admission date, license status (active, inactive, retired, suspended, disbarred), practice address (many states), law school attended, disciplinary history (public actions), and areas of practice (where disclosed). Zero PII — all professional credential and disciplinary data under state bar rules and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 51 state bar websites (California, Wisconsin, Texas, Florida, New York all confirmed publicly searchable), deduplicate multi-jurisdiction attorneys, normalize status codes and practice areas, flag disciplinary records. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($2,000-$10,000/year) or per-record pricing ($0.15-$0.40/record), leaving a clear gap for a one-time $99-$149 CSV. Audience size is massive: over 1.3 million licensed attorneys nationwide (including inactive licenses), creating a TAM of 10,000+ potential B2B buyers across LegalTech, CLE, research platforms, insurance, and marketing verticals. Score is 9 due to validated exceptionally high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors at premium pricing ($200-$295 baseline), confirmed public data availability across all 51 jurisdictions with state bar aggregation, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, massive attorney population (1.3M+), and five distinct B2B buyer segments with proven high-LTV purchasing behavior in LegalTech, insurance, and professional services markets.

data_wanted: All 50 state Bar Associations plus DC maintain public attorney license registries, accessible via state-specific Bar Association or Supreme Court licensing division websites with no authentication required for lookup. California State Bar Attorney Search (apps.calbar.ca.gov/attorney), Wisconsin State Bar (wisbar.org), Texas State Bar (texasbar.com), Florida Bar (floridabar.org), New York State Unified Court System Attorney Registration, and 46 additional state bar associations all provide public searchable databases. Key fields per license: attorney full name (first, middle initial, last), state bar number (format varies by state, typically 5-9 digits), admission date (initial bar admission in that state), license status (active, inactive, retired, suspended, disbarred, resigned), practice address (street, city, state, ZIP — availability varies by state; some bars list full address, others only city/state, some redact entirely per attorney privacy election), law school attended and graduation year, areas of practice or specializations (where voluntarily disclosed by attorney), disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, and reinstatements — private warnings not included), and multi-jurisdiction bar memberships (where cross-listed). Target all active and inactive licenses (exclude only disbarred, resigned with disciplinary charges, or revoked). Scope to individual attorneys only — exclude corporate law offices or legal services organizations. Approximately 1.3 million attorney licenses nationwide as of 2026 (note: many attorneys hold licenses in multiple states via reciprocity or admission on motion, so unique individual count is ~900K-1M). Target output: 1.3M rows, one per license (some individuals appear multiple times if licensed in multiple states). Data is 100% public per state bar rules and state Freedom of Information laws — attorney licensing and disciplinary records are public information under ABA Model Rules and state bar ethical codes.
